main_text.p: Collocatio argumentorum in singulis partibus.& prudentiam agnofcunt : qui gratias a-gunt: qui in amicorum fefe poteftate fu-turos pollicentur. Ad tractationem autem & collocationem harum fententiarum q; attinet, quatuor in refpondendo obfer-uandæ partes erunt. Exordium,quod con-ftabit, aut ἐπαναλήψει[?] breui repetitione & commendatione inftitutæ ab amico ex-hortationis. lib.2. epift.15. lib.10. epift. 4. lib.11. epift. 11. Aut reprehenfione & infe-ctatione maleuolorum.lib.11.epift.21.Aut excufatione negle&i in fcribendo officij. lib.10. epift.4. Deinde Propofitio, appro-batione facta adhortationis, & pollicita-tione eorum que à nobis requiruntur.lib. 2.epift.15. lib.10.epift.4.li.11.epift.11. Tum confirmatio, quæ rationes continebit & argumenta,quibus fcilicet impellamur vt exhortationi amici locum relinquamus, eaq; fumentur vel ab honeftate & vtilita-te ipfius adhortationis.lib.10.epift.4. Vel rerum & temporum conditione. lib.2.e-pift.15.Vel ingenio,moribus, confuetudi-ne noftra. lib.2. epift.15. Vel eius qui ad nos fcripfit,amore,fide,prudentia,autori-tate.lib.10.epift.4.lib.11.epift.21.Poftremò conclufio quæ abfoluetur [illegible, ~6 letters], & ἀξιώ- σει promissione & petitione.Nam & pol-lice-

page.notes: Marginal note in the left margin is set in italic and partly broken; "argumentorum" is a reading of the damaged word "g..mentorum". Greek words after "Exordium" and "conclusio" are only partly legible; the Greek before "promissione" was read as ἀξιώσει across a line break. The word after "abfoluetur" is Greek and not reliably read. The running text ends mid-word with "lice-" and continues on the next page.
